title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-33
notes:
West leads the ♠10 against 6♠. West's trump lead is won by South. South should cash the top hearts immediately and ruff a heart in dummy. The 3-3 break is good news but South is not out of the woods yet.

South could cash the ♦A for a club discard, ruff a diamond to the closed hand and play trumps from the top. The contract will make whenever trumps are 3-3.

However, West's lead of the ♠10 strongly suggests that East has a trump trick. If this is the case, South still has a chance by exiting with the fourth round of trump. If East has the ♣K and began with 1 or 2 diamonds he will be endplayed.

If South is willing to make the reasonable assumption that East has 4 trumps, there is a stronger line of play that does not depend on East's holding short diamonds. South should not cash dummy's ♦A. He should lead a small diamond instead and ruff in his hand. To prevent East from unblocking his spades and avoid being endplayed, South should be careful to ruff with the ♠4.

South cashes his top spades, revealing the expected 4-2 break. Despite East's efforts to unblock, South's ♠2 is just low enough to lose the lead to East. With East holding the ♣K, he is endplayed into giving South a way to dispose of his 2 club losers.
